decision.explanation: The claim posits that Alectinib has sensitivity/response activity in head and neck cancer patients harboring the EML4::ALK fusion with the ALK G1202R mutation. The available evidence (pmid-25727400:f01) is a preclinical study using NPM-ALK and EML4-ALK cellular models, not head and neck cancer patients. Furthermore, the study explicitly reports that the G1202R mutation is highly refractory (resistant) to Alectinib (RR = 27.9), directly contradicting the claim of sensitivity. The evidence is insufficient to support the claim in the specified disease context and direction.

citations.quote: Since the biological activity of ALK mutations extends beyond the specific type of fusion, both NPM-ALK- and EML4-ALK-positive cellular models were used. . . . In the activity profile of alectinib, we found three sensitive mutations (C1156Y, L1196M, and S1206Y), and three with varying degrees of resistance (Tables 3). In particular, G1202R was highly refractory to alectinib (RR = 27.9).
